title: Bitopological Lie Algebras: Properties and Examples
content: We introduce and study bitopological Lie algebras, namely Lie algebras equipped with two compatible vector-space topologies. The purpose is to develop an algebraic counterpart of bitopological Lie groups and to make precise the interaction between the Lie bracket and two topological structures. We begin by recalling the basic theory of bitopological spaces and Lie algebras. We then define pairwise continuous Lie brackets, bitopological Lie subalgebras, ideals, homomorphisms, isomorphisms, derivations, centers, and representations. Several basic structural properties are established. In particular, we investigate the continuity of the adjoint maps, the behavior of closures of subalgebras and ideals, kernels and images of bitopologically continuous homomorphisms, direct sums, quotients, and finite-dimensional examples. We also establish a natural relationship between a bitopological Lie group and its Lie algebra. Under suitable compatibility assumptions, the adjoint representation induces a pairwise continuous action on the corresponding bitopological Lie algebra. Several examples are presented, including abelian Lie algebras, the affine Lie algebra, matrix Lie algebras, Heisenberg Lie algebras, and Lie algebras endowed with weak and strong topologies. The theory developed here provides a foundation for further investigation of bitopological Lie groups, representations, Lie-symmetry algebras of differential equations, and optimal systems of Lie subalgebras.
